subject: alt-d
title: (R)ALT.D.------AFI.
description: Diagram in WAM-22, on the page where Braxton argues that notation in western art music produced 'the gradual inability of western musicians to function creatively without notation'. The subject (R)ALT-D — the reality of alternative definitions — is crossed with AFI (affinity insight); the (c) prefix on AFI marks the crossing relation, while (p) on IST-F marks the *point of activation* code (per Braxton's CODE notation, p13–14). AFI sits at the diagram's hub: it solid-links to ALT-D (the subject), to ATTN (attraction) which dashed-links to RT-INT-TR (reality initiative traits), to ALT-C-PG (alternative composite progressionalism) → INDIV-TD (individual tendencies), and to INFO-AF-B (information affinity basis). A *dashed* edge from AFI to (p)IST-F registers that affinity insight only conditionally activates as isolated focus. The argument: under western composer-medium conditions, alternative definitions reach reality only through affinity-insight, but affinity-insight itself fans out into multiple competing channels (attraction, alternative composite progressionalism, information affinity basis) and arrives at the point-of-activation only contingently — which structurally explains why western musicians so rarely produce alternative definitions outside the notational frame.
